chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from Sabbah al-Hadda', from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a group who went out on a journey. When they reached the place where shortening (salat) became obligatory for them, they shortened. When they had traveled two farsakhs, or three farsakhs, or four, a man lagged behind them, and their journey was not complete/straightforward except with him. So they stayed waiting for his arrival to them, and their journey was not complete except with his arrival. So they stayed upon that for days, not knowing whether they should continue in their journey or return. Is it befitting for them to complete the prayer or to persist in shortening it?

He (peace be upon him) said: If they had reached the distance of four farsakhs, let them persist in shortening, whether they stay or return; and if they had traveled less than four farsakhs, let them complete the prayer, whether they stay or return. So when they continue, let them shorten.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: Shortening the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs during travel
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: Farsakhs, a unit of distance used in Islamic jurisprudence for travel
key_terms.يُتِمُّوا: To complete (the prayer, i.e., pray four rak'ahs)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayer for travelers who wait for a companion after starting their journey?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of the 'traveler's status' (musafir) when a journey is paused, establishing that the four-farsakh threshold determines whether the shortening (qasr) or completion (tamm) of prayer remains in effect during the delay. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the travel state rather than mere physical movement, ensuring that the spiritual ease of the traveler is preserved even when stationary. This ruling underscores the practical application of divine mercy, allowing the group to maintain their relaxed prayer status provided they had already crossed the minimum distance before the interruption.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqu, from Muhammad Bin Aslam Al Jabaly, from Sabbah Al Haza’a, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws about a group which went out in a journey. So when they ended up to the place in which the shortening would be Obligated upon them, they shortened the Salāt. So when they came to be upon two Farsakhs (6 miles), or upon three Farsakhs (9 miles), or four, a man was left behind from them, their journey not remaining straight for them except with him. So they stayed awaiting his coming to them and the journey was not straight for them except with his coming to them. So they stayed upon that for days, not knowing whether they should be continuing in their journey or they should be dispersing. Is it befitting for them that they should be praying the complete Salāt, or they should be persisting upon their shortening?’

Heasws said: ‘If it was that the journey had reached four Farsakhs (12 miles), so let them stay upon their shortening, whether they stay or disperse; and if it was so that they had journeyed for less than four Farsakhs (12 miles), so let them pray the complete Salāt, whether they stay or disperse. So when they continue, so let them shorten’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqiy, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabaliy from Sabbah al-Hadhdha’ from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a people who are on a journey. When they arrived at the place where they were required to perform their Salah (prayer) in a reduced form, they reduced their Salah (prayer). After traveling two, three, or four farsakh, one of them without whom their journey could not be done remained behind. They waited for his arrival. Without him their journey was not possible. They stayed there for many days without knowing to go forward or return. Are they required to perform their Salah (prayer) complete or reduce it?’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If they have traveled four farsakh they reduce their Salah (prayer), regardless, they stay there or return. If they have traveled less than four farsakh, they perform their Salah (prayer) complete, regardless, they stay there or return.”’
